extracted.intended_audience: students, general readers, and scholars interested in postcolonial literature and literary theory
extracted.subtask_description: A broad encyclopaedic survey of postcolonial literature: definitions, key terms, critical approaches, major themes (nationalism, negritude, feminism, diaspora), regional developments, and representative authors and texts. Useful for analysing or situating creative writing in postcolonial contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: literature by people from formerly colonized countries
rubrics_metrics.description: Postcolonial literature is the literature by people from formerly colonized countries... Postcolonial literature often addresses the problems and consequences of the colonization and subsequent decolonization of a country, especially questions relating to the political and cultural independence of formerly subjugated people, and themes such as racialism and colonialism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a primary scope criterion: works that foreground the historical/political legacy of colonization, questions of political and cultural independence, and related themes (race, colonialism) fall squarely within postcolonial literature. Examples and regions covered range globally (all continents except Antarctica).

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiation/subversion of Euro‑American ideologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Pramod Nayar defines postcolonial literature as 'that which negotiates with, contests, and subverts Euro-American ideologies and representations'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a text actively contests, reinterprets, or subverts Euro‑American portrayals and power structures. 'Writing back' to European/imperial narratives is a common indicator. Works that simply reproduce Eurocentric viewpoints without critique are weaker on this dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing back to the colonial centre ('writes back')
rubrics_metrics.description: It is at its most overt in texts that write back to the European canon (Thieme 2001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess intertextual strategies that respond to, revise, or subvert canonical European works (e.g., Wide Sargasso Sea as a prequel/response to Jane Eyre). A successful 'writing back' text will reframe the original narrative's assumptions, center colonized perspectives, or expose colonial violence/omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance of the prefix 'post-' (hyphenation framing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The significance of the prefix 'post-' in 'postcolonial' is a matter of contention... 'Post-colonial' (with a hyphen) signifies a period that comes chronologically 'after' colonialism. 'Postcolonial,' on the other hand, signals the persisting impact of colonization across time periods and geographical regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose terminology deliberately: using 'post-colonial' frames works as chronologically after empire; 'postcolonial' foregrounds ongoing colonial effects. Be wary of homogenizing distinct colonial histories through careless label use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colonial discourse analysis (Orientalism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Postcolonial literary theory re-examines colonial and postcolonial literature, especially concentrating upon the social discourse between the colonizer and the colonized that shaped and produced the literature. In Orientalism (1978), Edward Said analyzed ... exploring how they shaped and were influenced by the societal fantasy of European racial superiority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate representations of the 'Other', how texts produce/sustain colonial stereotypes, and how power relations are encoded in discourse. Use Said's framework to interrogate authorial position, narrative voice, and implicit assumptions about race/civility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bhabha's concepts: hybridity, third‑space, mimicry, ambivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: Homi K. Bhabha has developed key concepts such as hybridity, third-space, mimicry, difference, and ambivalence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these concepts as analytic criteria: assess how texts show cultural mixing (hybridity), spaces of negotiation (third-space), ambivalent imitation (mimicry), and the destabilization of fixed identities. These features often signal complex postcolonial subjectivities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationalism and the role of literature in national identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Language and literature were factors in consolidating this sense of national identity to resist the impact of colonialism... Postcolonial literature not only helped consolidate national identity in anti-colonial struggles but also critiqued the European colonial pedigree of nationalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a work builds or critiques national imaginaries: does it consolidate a shared identity (sometimes excluding minorities) or problematize nationhood and the European models it may replicate? Consider discourse on imagined communities, exclusion of marginalized voices, and the mediums (press, novels) that shape national narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negritude, Pan‑Africanism, and debates on racial solidarity vs diasporic formation
rubrics_metrics.description: Négritude is a literary and ideological philosophy... Pan‑Africanism was a movement among English-speaking black intellectuals... Paul Gilroy argued black cultural forms were diasporic and transnational formations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating African/Francophone texts, consider whether they advance racial solidarity/negritude or instead emphasize diasporic, transnational experiences. Both are legitimate postcolonial responses but point to different political and aesthetic priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti‑conquest narratives and their risks
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'anti-conquest narrative' recasts the indigenous inhabitants of colonized countries as victims rather than foes of the colonisers... This depicts the colonised people in a more human light but risks absolving colonisers of responsibility by assuming that native inhabitants were 'doomed' to their fate. Pratt analyzes 'anti-conquest' as a strategy that secures the innocence of the imperialist even as he exercises his dominance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess narrative positioning: does a supposedly sympathetic account inadvertently erase indigenous agency or exculpate imperial actors? Avoid celebrating portrayals that humanize natives only to deny their political subjectivity or responsibility of colonizers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postcolonial feminism: intersection of gender, race, and colonial effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Postcolonial feminism ... accounts for the way that racism and the long-lasting political, economic, and cultural effects of colonialism affect non-white, non-Western women. Postcolonial feminism is not simply a subset of postcolonial studies or another variety of feminism. Rather, it seeks to act as an intervention that changes the assumptions of both postcolonial and feminist studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate representation of women through an intersectional lens that considers colonialism's specific impacts. Strong postcolonial feminist texts decolonize imagination/society and address women's roles in globalized contexts, migration, and precarity (examples: Nawal El Saadawi, Chimamanda Adichie).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language choice and writing in colonizer's language vs indigenous languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Chinua Achebe wrote his novels in English and defended the use of English... Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o ... formerly working in English and now working in Gikuyu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the implications of language choice: writing in a colonial language may reach wider audiences but raises questions about cultural autonomy; writing in indigenous languages can be an act of resistance and reclamation. Consider audience, politics, and intended readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of dialect / 'nation language' / creole
rubrics_metrics.description: One unique and pervasive characteristic of Caribbean literature is the use of 'dialect' forms of the national language, often termed creole... Many Caribbean authors in their writing switch liberally between the local variation – now commonly termed nation language – and the standard form of the language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate register shifts and code‑switching as authenticating strategies: use of nation language/creole can assert local identity and challenge colonial linguistic hierarchies. Consider how dialect shapes voice, characterization, and cultural specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of oral traditions, proverbs, and oratory
rubrics_metrics.description: Achebe's novels focus on the traditions of Igbo society... His style relies heavily on the Igbo oral tradition, and combines straightforward narration with representations of folk stories, proverbs, and oratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for formal strategies that integrate oral forms (myth, proverb, storytelling techniques) to root narratives in indigenous cultural practices and to contest Western narrative norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of marginalized voices and plurality within national literatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Postcolonial literature... critiqued the European colonial pedigree of nationalism. The homogeneous nation was built on European models by the exclusion of marginalized voices... Part of the problem is that English literature has been seen within the greater context of English writing in the world, and has, because of English's global position as lingua franca, not been seen as autonomous or indigenous to South Africa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether texts include or silence minority/indigenous perspectives. Strong postcolonial works make space for plurality and problematize monolithic national narratives; weak ones replicate exclusionary discourses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reclamation of culture, diaspora, and loss (themes common in Pacific and diaspora writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reclamation of culture, loss of culture, diaspora, all themes common to postcolonial literature, are present within the collective Pacific writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate themes of cultural reclamation, diasporic identity, dislocation, and the negotiation between homeland traditions and metropolitan life. These are central motifs in many regional postcolonial literatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with Western canonical works via rewriting or prequels
rubrics_metrics.description: Jean Rhys is best known for her 1966 novel Wide Sargasso Sea, which was written as a prequel to Charlotte Brontë's Jane Eyre. The novel deals with themes of women living in a patriarchal society, race, and assimilation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess intertextual strategies that retell canonical stories from colonized perspectives, expose omissions or racism in originals, and thereby critique literary history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and genre choices reflecting historical and political context
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first half of the 20th century, epics largely dominated black writing: historical novels, such as Mhudi... and epic plays... Female literature in the African languages is severely limited because of the strong influence of patriarchy, but over the last decade or two society has changed much and it can be expected that more female voices will emerge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how choice of genre (epic, historical novel, memoir, poetry, drama) is used to address history, identity, resistance, and gender. Evaluate whether the form supports the political aims and cultural contexts of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology evolution and the limits of labels (commonwealth literature vs postcolonial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the term 'postcolonial literature' gained currency ... 'commonwealth literature' was used to refer to writing in English from colonies... The succeeding generation of postcolonial critics ... took issue with the 'commonwealth' label for separating non-British writing from 'English' language literature written in Britain. They also suggested that texts in this category frequently presented a short-sighted view on the legacy of colonialism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When categorizing works, be cautious about inherited labels; consider historical usage, who the label includes/excludes, and whether it flattens differences. Prefer more precise descriptors when possible (regional, linguistic, or thematic tags).
